extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: scientists, students, instrument buyers, and academic administrators (early-20th-century Britain)
extracted.subtask_description: A journal supplement to Nature containing book notices, instrument advertisements and usage guidance, subscription and advertisement submission rules, and university admissions/bursary notices. The page mixes promotional material with short procedural instructions and product specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct use of the Anglemeter for measuring heights (accessible objects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure for measuring the height of an accessible object (e.g., a tall pole) with the Anglemeter: 'First set the pinhole to the angle marked 45°. The Anglemeter is held in a vertical plane, and a spot on the pole on a level with the eye of the observer is sighted, through the pinhole, exactly over the line on the mirror. Then pace backwards, keeping the pointer set at this angle until you can get the reflection of the top of the pole on the cross line in the mirror.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the reflection aligns on the cross line the angle between line of sight and the reflection is 45°, and consequently the line made from the object to this spot will be equal to the height of the top of the pole above the observer's eye. Practice first with objects not too far distant and not too small. The instrument is promoted as a simple, inexpensive surveying tool for students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct use of the Anglemeter for measuring inaccessible objects (two-angle method)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the object is inaccessible a second reading is necessary: 'a base line must be measured and angles taken at each end.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For surveying a large field use the same method but take sights to two objects and read the angle between them on the instrument (example given: sight one chimney then slide until the reflection of the other appears; read the scale to get the angle, e.g., 65°). The text notes the Anglemeter can yield surveys as accurate as with a chain and avoids difficulties from surface inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anglemeter reading/precision and scale interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: How to interpret the Anglemeter scale and precision: 'When objects are seen in the mirror the angle made by its direction with the line of sight is twice that through which the radial arm is moved, in accordance with the ordinary laws of the reflection of light. The quadrant is therefore marked as 180°, and the smaller divisions proportionally.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reading recorded is then the exact angle to be observed. 'One-fifth of a degree can be easily read by this device.' The advertisement recommends practice and emphasizes the instrument's educational value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission rules for Nature advertisements and editorial communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where to send correspondence for Nature: 'NOTICE. — Advertisements and business letters for Nature should be addressed to the Publishers; Editorial communications to the Editor. The telegraphic address of Nature is "Phusis," London.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subscription and advertisement charging information is provided (rates for yearly/half-yearly/quarterly subscriptions, and charges for advertisements by lines and by page fractions). Payment instructions: 'Cheques and Money Orders payable to MACMILLAN CO., Limited. OFFICE: ST. MARTIN'S STREET, LONDON. W.C.' (advertisement rates and some numeric values appear in the text).

rubrics_metrics.name: University of St. Andrews admissions and bursary application requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural and eligibility requirements for admissions and bursary competitions at the University of St. Andrews: 'The Preliminary Examination, with which the competitions for Bursaries are combined, will commence on September 27. Schedules of application for admission will be supplied by the Secretary, and must be returned to him before September 14.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bursary details: 'There are forty-two Bursaries vacant (six of which are open to second year students and two to fourth year students) ranging in value from £40 to £16 5s. Of these twenty-two are tenable by men only, fifteen (fourteen of which are restricted to students who intend to enter the Medical Profession) by women only, and four (including two Spence Bursaries...) by either men or women.' Grants not exceeding [amount garbled in text] may be assigned to fourth-year students who wish to take a Degree with Honours. Ten scholarships (values given) will be open to competition during the session, with some open to either sex.

rubrics_metrics.name: St. Mary's College (Divinity) bursary examination rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Dates and formal rules for bursary competitions at St. Mary's College: 'This College will be opened on Monday, October 14. The Examinations for Bursaries will be held on October 11 and 12. Intimation of candidature is not necessary. There are six competitive Bursaries vacant, ranging in value from ... to £13.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At the close of the Session one Scholarship of £30, one of £21, and one of £14 will be open to competition. Classes are open to students of both sexes and include a range of subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specifications for the Student's Resistance Box (teaching apparatus)
rubrics_metrics.description: Product/specification requirements for a resistance coil set designed for teaching: 'This set of coils has been made specially for teaching purposes. Students can see all cells and connections, as the case is a thick glass cylinder, ebonite top, heavy blocks, well-fitting plugs, and mahogany base.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coils adjusted to '02% (0.02%?), 1 ohm to 100 ohms. Price given with Ebonite Capped Plugs, and a descriptive leaflet is available on application to THE WEST LONDON SCIENTIFIC APPARATUS CO. (the text includes price information).
